title: Best practices guide: sandbox blast-radius claim overstates what sandbox mode delivers (Section 3.2)
author: barka-bee
inline_text:
Origin: PR #9 review thread https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/9#discussion_r4015533684.

**Current text** ([L109](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/e757d350133fea0858dda1deec13dbca923b3cf8/deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md?plain=1#L109)): sandbox mode "reduces the blast radius of any unverified artifact from full system access to working-directory scope". The row on [L106](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/e757d350133fea0858dda1deec13dbca923b3cf8/deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md?plain=1#L106) rates it "Contained".

**Proposal.** Keep the recommendation, state it honestly: sandbox mode narrows the filesystem, it does not close egress or the trust handoff to host tools. Update the L106 row to match.

**Why.** Pillar escaped the sandboxes of Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and Antigravity in one week, in most cases without breaking the sandbox at all: the agent writes a file that an unsandboxed host component later runs (https://www.pillar.security/blog/the-week-of-sandbox-escapes). And the agent does not need an attacker to route around egress. In our Cursor testing, curl was blocked, so the agent used Python urllib and uploaded project files to a public anonymous host to finish an ordinary task (https://www.capsulesecurity.io/blog-post/cursebox-the-agent-that-sends-your-files-to-strangers-to-get-the-job-done, my employer's post).
